title: ArXiv: 'Verify Before You Commit: Towards Faithful Reasoning in LLM Agents via Self-Auditing'
description: Paper introduces a self-auditing mechanism for LLM agents that verifies reasoning before committing to actions, helping prevent hallucinations and improving reliability in decision-making processes. The approach addresses critical trust issues in autonomous AI agents.
author: Wenhao Yuan, Chenchen Lin, Jian Chen, Jinfeng Xu, Xuehe Wang, Edith Cheuk Han Ngai

title: ArXiv: 'SUPERNOVA: Eliciting General Reasoning in LLMs with Reinforcement Learning on Natural Instructions'
description: Presents SUPERNOVA, a reinforcement learning approach that elicits general reasoning capabilities in LLMs through natural instructions. The method aims to improve LLM performance on complex reasoning tasks by training on diverse instruction sets.
author: Ashima Suvarna, Kendrick Phan, Mehrab Beikzadeh, Hritik Bansal, Saadia Gabriel

title: ArXiv: 'KnowU-Bench: Towards Interactive, Proactive, and Personalized Mobile Agent Evaluation'
description: Introduces a comprehensive benchmark for evaluating mobile agents across interactive, proactive, and personalized dimensions. The work addresses the need for standardized evaluation frameworks in mobile AI agent development.
author: Tongbo Chen, Zhengxi Lu, Zhan Xu, Guocheng Shao, Shaohan Zhao, Fei Tang, Yong Du, Kaitao Song, Yizhou Liu, Yuchen Yan, Wenqi Zhang, Xu Tan, Weiming Lu, Jun Xiao, Yueting Zhuang, Yongliang Shen

title: ArXiv: 'SkillClaw: Let Skills Evolve Collectively with Agentic Evolver'
description: Presents a framework that enables skills to evolve collectively through an agentic evolver. This approach allows AI systems to develop and refine skills in a collaborative manner, improving overall agent capabilities.
author: Ziyu Ma, Shidong Yang, Yuxiang Ji, Xucong Wang, Yong Wang, Yiming Hu, Tongwen Huang, Xiangxiang Chu

title: ArXiv: 'Don't Overthink It: Inter-Rollout Action Agreement as a Free Adaptive-Compute Signal for LLM Agents'
description: Introduces an approach that uses inter-rollout action agreement as a signal for adaptive compute allocation in LLM agents. The method helps balance reasoning depth with computational efficiency, preventing overthinking while maintaining performance.
author: Khushal Sethi

title: ArXiv: 'PASK: Toward Intent-Aware Proactive Agents with Long-Term Memory'
description: PASK introduces a framework for intent-aware proactive agents with long-term memory capabilities. The system enables AI agents to understand user intentions over extended interactions and take proactive actions based on accumulated context.
author: Zhifei Xie, Zongzheng Hu, Fangda Ye, Xin Zhang, Haobo Chai, Zihang Liu, Pengcheng Wu, Guibin Zhang, Yue Liao, Xiaobin Hu, Deheng Ye, Chunyan Miao, Shuicheng Yan

title: ArXiv: 'Lightweight LLM Agent Memory with Small Language Models'
description: Addresses the challenge of memory efficiency in LLM agents by proposing a lightweight memory system using small language models. The approach reduces computational costs while maintaining effective memory capabilities for AI agents.
author: Jiaquan Zhang, Chaoning Zhang, Shuxu Chen, Zhenzhen Huang, Pengcheng Zheng, Zhicheng Wang, Ping Guo, Fan Mo, Sung-Ho Bae, Jie Zou, Jiwei Wei, Yang Yang

title: ArXiv: 'SEARL: Joint Optimization of Policy and Tool Graph Memory for Self-Evolving Agents'
description: SEARL introduces a framework for jointly optimizing policy and tool graph memory in self-evolving agents. The system enables AI agents to adapt and improve their capabilities over time through continuous learning and optimization.
author: Xinshun Feng, Xinhao Song, Lijun Li, Gongshen Liu, Jing Shao

title: ArXiv: 'ACIArena: Toward Unified Evaluation for Agent Cascading Injection'
description: Provides a unified evaluation framework for agent cascading injection, addressing the challenge of evaluating complex multi-agent interactions. The work aims to standardize evaluation methodologies for cascading agent systems.
author: Hengyu An, Minxi Li, Jinghuai Zhang, Naen Xu, Chunyi Zhou, Changjiang Li, Xiaogang Xu, Tianyu Du, Shouling Ji

title: ArXiv: 'SAT: Balancing Reasoning Accuracy and Efficiency with Stepwise Adaptive Thinking'
description: SAT introduces a stepwise adaptive thinking approach that balances reasoning accuracy and efficiency in AI systems. The method allows AI models to adapt their reasoning depth based on task complexity and available computational resources.
author: Weiyang Huang, Xuefeng Bai, Kehai Chen, Xinyang Chen, Yibin Chen, Weili Guan, Min Zhang

title: ArXiv: 'Beyond Isolated Tasks: A Framework for Evaluating Coding Agents on Sequential Software Evolution'
description: This framework evaluates coding agents on sequential software evolution tasks, moving beyond isolated code generation to assess performance on complex, multi-stage software development processes. The work addresses the need for more comprehensive evaluation of AI coding assistants.
author: KN Ajay Shastry, Ganesh Senrayan, Shrey Satapara, Pranoy Panda, Chaitanya Devaguptapu

title: ArXiv: 'IndustryCode: A Benchmark for Industry Code Generation'
description: IndustryCode introduces a benchmark specifically designed for evaluating code generation in industry settings. The work addresses the gap between academic code generation benchmarks and real-world industrial requirements.
author: Puyu Zeng, Zhaoxi Wang, Zhixu Duan, Liang Feng, Shaobo Wang, Cunxiang Wang, Jinghang Wang, Bing Zhao, Hu Wei, Linfeng Zhang

title: Simon Willison: 'Vulnerability Research Is Cooked'
description: Thomas Ptacek's analysis of how frontier AI models are revolutionizing vulnerability research and exploit development. Argues that coding agents will drastically alter both the practice and economics of vulnerability research within months, with agents able to 'find me zero days' by leveraging baked-in knowledge, pattern matching abilities, and brute force searching.
author: Simon Willison (covering Thomas Ptacek)

title: Simon Willison: 'Eight years of wanting, three months of building with AI'
description: A deep dive into Lalit Maganti's experience building syntaqlite (SQLite linting and verification tools) over three months after eight years of planning. Explores the pros and cons of AI-assisted development, including insights on how AI helps overcome initial technical hurdles but can sometimes hinder architectural decision-making.
author: Simon Willison (covering Lalit Maganti)

title: Simon Willison: 'Google AI Edge Gallery'
description: Review of Google's official iPhone app for running Gemma 4 models directly on device. Highlights the app's effectiveness with the 2.54GB E2B model, features like image questioning and audio transcription, and the 'skills' demo showing tool calling capabilities against interactive widgets.
author: Simon Willison

title: Simon Willison: 'GLM-5.1: Towards Long-Horizon Tasks'
description: Analysis of Z.ai's 754B parameter GLM-5.1 model, featuring a pelican-on-a-bicycle test that demonstrated the model's ability to generate complete HTML pages with SVG animations and CSS. Includes follow-up on fixing animation issues and additional creative outputs.
author: Simon Willison

title: Simon Willison: 'Anthropic's Project Glasswing—restricting Claude Mythos to security researchers—sounds necessary to me'
description: Discussion of Anthropic's decision to restrict access to Claude Mythos model under Project Glasswing, limiting it to security researchers. Explores the implications of this restricted release approach for advanced AI models.
author: Simon Willison

title: Simon Willison: 'Meta's new model is Muse Spark, and meta.ai chat has some interesting tools'
description: Coverage of Meta's Muse Spark model announcement and analysis of the tools available in meta.ai chat. Discusses the model's hosted (not open weights) nature and the private API preview status.
author: Simon Willison

title: Simon Willison: 'GitHub doesn't tell you the repo size in the UI, but it's available in the CORS-friendly API'
description: Technical post about discovering repository size through GitHub's CORS-friendly API, with a mention of fixing an issue with asgi-gzip compression affecting text/event-stream responses in Datasette.
author: Simon Willison

title: Hacker News: 'Eight years of wanting, three months of building with AI' - Extended Discussion
description: Extended Hacker News discussion (757 points) on Simon Willison's post about AI-assisted development. Commenters debate: (1) Code quality relevance in AI era - whether it matters more or less, (2) 'Vibe coding' productivity vs technical debt, (3) AI as accelerator vs engineer replacement, (4) Democratization of software development, (5) Comparison to historical technology shifts (printing press, internet), (6) Testing challenges with AI-generated code, (7) Future of software engineering profession. Strong consensus that AI is a tool requiring human oversight, with diverse opinions on long-term implications.
author: Hacker News Community (discussion on Simon Willison's post)

title: Simon Willison: 'Tool: Cleanup Claude Code Paste'
description: Niche tool for cleaning up Claude Code terminal output by removing the ❯ prompt character, fixing whitespace from line wrapping, and joining broken lines into readable paragraphs. Addresses pain points of copying terminal prompts.
author: Simon Willison
